reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight is that optimal resource allocation reduces to finding equilibrium ratios among measurable physical quantities. This is achieved through a 'price system' that equates marginal rates of substitution across all feasible alternatives. The primitives formalize this idea: maximizing total value (primal), setting equality constraints (duality), and ensuring positive measurable outcomes. Failure occurs when preferences become non-convex or when computational limits prevent full optimization, leading to suboptimal allocations.
